description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. Tender pieces of marinated chicken are simmered to perfection in a mildly spiced, buttery gravy. This iconic dish offers a delightful balance of sweet and savory flavors, making it a favorite across the globe.

ingredients.notes: soaked in warm water for 15 minutes

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, lemon juice, and salt to taste. Mix thoroughly to ensure the chicken is well coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally for 2-4 hours, to allow the flavors to deepen.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee or unsalted butter in a large heavy-bottomed pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook the chicken until it is nicely browned on all sides and about 70-80% cooked through, approximately 5-7 minutes. Remove the cooked chicken from the pan and set it aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of ghee or unsalted butter. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté over medium heat until it becomes soft, translucent, and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato and Cashew Mixture
instructions.text: Add the canned crushed tomatoes, soaked cashew nuts, remaining 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, sugar, and salt to the pan with the onions and ginger garlic paste. Stir everything together well. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the raw tomato flavor mellows.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked sauce mixture from the pan into a blender. Blend until it achieves a completely smooth and creamy consistency. If needed, add a small amount of water to aid blending. For an extra silky texture, strain the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on any solids to extract maximum flavor.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the smooth, strained sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the previously cooked chicken pieces, the heavy cream, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon garam masala. Stir in the crushed kasoori methi. Simmer the butter chicken for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully and the chicken to finish cooking through completely. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish the rich and creamy Butter Chicken with fresh chopped cilantro and an extra drizzle of heavy cream, if desired, just before serving. Enjoy this authentic Murgh Makhani hot with warm naan bread, roti, or fluffy basmati rice for a truly satisfying Indian meal.

tips: For truly authentic flavor and tender chicken, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer the marinade time, the more deeply the spices penetrate the meat, enhancing both taste and texture.

Kashmiri red chili powder is essential for the vibrant red color of Butter Chicken without excessive heat. If unavailable, use a combination of paprika for color and a tiny pinch of cayenne pepper for a mild kick. Soaking cashews is crucial for achieving a smooth, rich, and creamy sauce texture.

Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day as the flavors continue to meld and deepen. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave, adding a splash of water or cream if needed.
article:
Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani: The Ultimate Indian Lunch Recipe

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian creation is more than just a meal; it's a culinary experience, a symphony of rich flavors, and a testament to the warmth of Indian cuisine. Renowned for its silky-smooth tomato and butter-based sauce, tender pieces of marinated chicken, and a subtle yet satisfying spice profile, it has earned its place as a global favorite, especially for a comforting and flavorful Indian lunch. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore exotic flavors, mastering this dish is a rewarding journey into the heart of Indian gastronomy.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant, it was born out of a desire to utilize leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich, creamy tomato gravy. The result was a revolutionary dish that quickly gained popularity across India and eventually the world. At its core, Murgh Makhani features succulent pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoor-cooked, though pan-seared or grilled works too) bathed in a vibrant orange-red sauce. This sauce is a delicate balance of tangy tomatoes, aromatic ginger and garlic, a medley of Indian spices, and the luxurious richness of butter and cream. It’s a dish celebrated for its mild heat, incredible depth of flavor, and its unparalleled creamy texture, making it an irresistible choice for any meal, particularly a satisfying Indian lunch.

## Ingredients You Need

Crafting authentic Butter Chicken requires a few key components that contribute to its distinctive taste and texture.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Murgh Makhani Sauce:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp ground coriander
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1 cup tomato puree (or canned crushed tomatoes)
*   1/2 cup cashew paste (soaked cashews blended with a little water)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1/4 cup water (or chicken broth)
*   1 tsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1 tsp sugar (optional, to balance tang)
*   Salt to taste
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish

## Step-by-Step Instructions

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours.
2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a little oil in a pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces and cook until they are browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
3.  **Prepare the Sauce Base:** In the same pan, melt the butter with the oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes.
4.  **Add Aromatics and Spices:** Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the red chili powder, turmeric, ground coriander, and garam masala. Sauté for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning.
5.  **Simmer the Sauce:** Pour in the tomato puree, cashew paste, and water/broth. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.
6.  **Blend (Optional but Recommended):** For an extra smooth sauce, carefully transfer the mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Return the blended sauce to the pan.
7.  **Finish the Butter Chicken:** Stir in the heavy cream, kasuri methi, and sugar (if using). Add the cooked chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the sauce. Adjust salt to taste.
8.  **Garnish and Serve:** Garnish generously with fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marinating time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be, enhancing the overall Butter Chicken experience.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use fresh, ripe tomatoes or a good quality canned tomato puree for the best sauce base. Fresh ginger-garlic paste also makes a significant difference.
*   **Blend for Smoothness:** While optional, blending the sauce after it has simmered creates that signature restaurant-style smooth and velvety texture. A stick blender can make this easier directly in the pot.
*   **Balance Flavors:** Taste and adjust. The sugar helps balance the tanginess of the tomatoes, and a pinch more salt or spice can elevate the dish to perfection. Don't be afraid to experiment to suit your palate.
*   **Kasuri Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is crucial for authentic flavor. Rub it between your palms before adding it to release its aromatic oils. It provides a unique depth that defines Murgh Makhani.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is wonderfully versatile and pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments. For a classic Indian lunch, serve it hot with fluffy basmati rice, warm naan bread, or rotis to soak up every last drop of the luscious sauce. A side of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and spices) or a simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, and onion) provides a refreshing contrast to the richness of the curry.

## Variations and Substitutions

This adaptable recipe allows for several variations. For a vegetarian alternative, substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables. If you’re not a fan of cashews, you can use blanched almonds or skip them, though they contribute to the sauce’s richness. For a dairy-free version, use coconut cream instead of heavy cream and a plant-based butter alternative. While traditional Butter Chicken calls for specific spices, feel free to adjust the chili powder to your preferred level of heat.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Is Butter Chicken spicy?**
Traditionally, Butter Chicken is known for its mild, creamy, and subtly sweet profile rather than being overtly spicy. The heat comes from red chili powder, which can be adjusted to personal preference. Kashmiri chili powder is often used for its vibrant color with minimal heat.

**Can I make Butter Chicken ahead of time?**
Absolutely! Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani often tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. You can prepare the entire dish and refrigerate it for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop, adding a splash of water or cream if the sauce has thickened too much.

**What's the difference between Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala?**
While both are popular creamy tomato-based chicken curries, there are distinct differences. Butter Chicken typically has a milder, sweeter, and richer flavor profile due to a higher proportion of butter and cream. Chicken Tikka Masala often features more pronounced spices, a tangier tomato base, and usually incorporates bell peppers and onions, offering a bolder, spicier taste.

**Can I freeze Butter Chicken?**
Yes, Butter Chicken freezes well. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer it to an airtight container and freeze for up to 2-3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently, stirring frequently.

Embrace the joy of cooking this classic Indian lunch recipe. Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a dish that truly satisfies, bringing comfort and exquisite flavor to your table. Its creamy texture and delicate balance of spices make it an unforgettable culinary journey, perfect for sharing with family and friends.
